content: Estrogens may diminish the serum IGF-1 response to somapacitan, potentially necessitating higher doses of somapacitan. Refer to the drug monograph for initial dosing recommendations and monitor patients closely. St. John’s Wort can reduce the efficacy or levels of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative therapies, and monitor closely. Streptomycin, sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, sulfisoxazole, teicoplanin, temocillin, tetracycline, tigecycline, tobramycin, trimethoprim, and vancomycin may decrease the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. Tacrolimus, teniposide, tolvaptan, verapamil, voriconazole, and zafirlukast may increase the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter or affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tesamorelin may reduce the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering metabolism. Monitor closely, as this may decrease efficacy. Trazodone may reduce the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is considered minor, with unknown clinical significance. Estrogens and progestins may reduce the therapeutic effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and associated adverse effects. Monitor closely. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens are contraindicated in pregnant women and not recommended for premenopausal women or those of reproductive potential due to the risk of fetal harm. There is no evidence of increased risk of birth defects from exposure to combined hormonal contraceptives before conception or during early pregnancy. However, there are no data on bazedoxifene use in pregnancy to assess the risk of adverse developmental outcomes. Animal studies suggest bazedoxifene may impair female fertility, but clinical fertility studies have not been conducted. Estrogens are present in human milk and may reduce milk production in breastfeeding women, particularly before lactation is well-established. There is no data on the presence of bazedoxifene in human or animal breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. Based on its mechanism of action, bazedoxifene may interfere with estrogen’s role in mammary tissue during lactation. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Estrogens, alone or with progestins, have rarely caused serious side effects. Discuss the risks and benefits of hormone therapy with your doctor. Estrogens can increase the risk of uterine (endometrial) cancer, but the bazedoxifene in this product may help reduce this risk. In postmenopausal women, estrogens (with or without progestins) increase the risk of breast/ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The risk of these side effects depends on the dose and duration of estrogen use. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration necessary. Regularly consult your doctor (e.g., every 3 to 6 months) to determine if continued use is needed. Long-term users should undergo regular physical exams (e.g., annually) as directed by their doctor. This medication combines conjugated estrogens and bazedoxifene (an estrogen agonist/antagonist). It is used in women with a uterus to alleviate menopausal symptoms (e.g., hot flashes, vaginal dryness) and prevent postmenopausal bone loss (osteoporosis). Conjugated estrogens reduce menopausal symptoms caused by decreased estrogen production, while bazedoxifene acts as a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) in specific tissues. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. To prevent stomach upset, take it with food or immediately after a meal. Swallow the tablets whole; do not crush or chew them. Take it regularly at the same time each day to maximize its benefits. Common side effects include stomach upset, nausea/vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, and weight changes. This medication may increase blood pressure and rarely cause serious blood clot-related issues (e.g., heart attack, stroke, pulmonary embolism, or deep vein thrombosis). Serious allergic reactions are rare. Contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to conjugated estrogens or bazedoxifene, or if you have other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or tobacco use, as these increase the risk of blood clots, especially when taking estrogen products. Inform your doctor if you have recently had or will undergo surgery or if you will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., long flights), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots. This medication may cause melasma (blotchy, dark skin patches). Limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing outdoors. Nearsighted individuals or contact lens users may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing lenses. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. Estrogens pass into breast milk and may reduce its quality and quantity. It is unknown if bazedoxifene passes into breast milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use (prescription, nonprescription, and herbal) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. In case of overdose, call emergency services (911) or a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Once the foil pouch is opened, the U.S. product expires after 60 days, and the Canadian product expires after 45 days. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted while taking this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-exams and report any lumps immediately. Maintain all medical and lab appointments. Lifestyle changes, such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking, can help prevent or manage high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, heart disease, and stroke. Mental exercises (e.g., reading, puzzles) may help prevent dementia. For healthy bones, engage in weight-bearing exercise, avoid smoking, limit alcohol, and consume adequate calcium and vitamin D.
